description: Passive joint moments, one row per joint. A measured row gives, for each direction away from neutral, the onset angle (rad) and polynomial stiffness [k0 Nm/rad, k1 Nm/rad^2, k2 Nm/rad^3] of the restoring moment M = -(k0 x + k1 x^2 + k2 x^3) sign-adjusted per side, with x the displacement beyond the onset. Gap rows list where values could come from; no value is used without a verified source. The measured rows are neutral-centred linear stiffness (onset 0): they act over the whole joint range, not only at its end, and are validated only inside valid_range. They do not by themselves model end-range stiffening, so they will not stop a controller from resting on a hard joint limit; an end-range row needs its own source or an explicit, documented extrapolation. Every applied row has a source_curve; its springs are fitted to the residual (source curve minus the model's own passive muscle moment at act = 0, at the source's posture; only its restoring part), per side of the residual's equilibrium by non-negative least squares over fit.range_rad (scripts/fit_passive_moments.py); onsets are absolute joint angles. Every row is scales_with 'none' (measured stiffness is kept unless a subject measurement exists); scales_with is provenance metadata for later subject scaling. The model itself is the generated block of myoarm_r_tendon.xml written from this table by scripts/fit_passive_moments.py; every measured and assumed row is applied (the status is provenance). A row with a damping entry sets that joint's damping (N m s/rad), written by the same script into myoarm_r_chain.xml; the other joints keep their class damping.

armature.method: Smallest value (of 4e-4, 5e-4, 6e-4 on each CMC axis, with MP 2e-4 to 4e-4) with no period-2 oscillation over 120 random thumb poses and random subsets of the thumb muscles at activation 1 at the 2 ms Euler step. joints.notes: Intrinsic component only (Knutson Eq. 2, Table 1 medians of 8 healthy subjects; units N cm, 1/deg, deg; theta = MCP flexion). The extrinsic component (Eq. 3, wrist dependent) belongs to the extrinsic muscle-tendon units and is not added. Validation: MyoHand's extrinsic index muscles (FDS2, FDP2, EDC2, EIP) give at most 1.2 N cm passive MCP moment over MCP 0-90 deg and wrist -60..60 deg, against Knutson's extrinsic fit of up to 30 N cm (e.g. -30 N cm at MCP 90 deg, wrist flexed 60 deg): the model lacks the extrinsic passive tension (tenodesis), so with the intrinsic curve alone the relaxed MCP settles near its intrinsic equilibrium (~55 deg flexion) instead of ~27 deg (intrinsic + extrinsic at wrist 0). The intrinsic muscles (RI2, LU_RB2, UI_UB2) add little passive moment. RI2's path used to jump by 7 mm between MCP 10 and 15 deg (its insertion entered the 2ndmcp wrap cylinder, and the sidesite forced a dorsal wrap below that) and gave -5..-9 N cm (extension) at MCP 0-10 deg; RI2 now runs without that wrap, continuous and within its lengthrange.

joints.notes: Assumption: no moment-angle curve of the CMC4/5 joints is published. The end-range load of El-Shennawy et al. 2001 (22 N) on MyoHand's CMC5-to-MCP5 lever (43.8 mm) gives about 0.96 N m at the end of the passive range; the row is a linear stiffness that reaches that moment at the model's flexion and extension limits (k = 0.964 N m / limit). The paper gives arcs only and does not say where on the pin the load acted, so the moment is a lower bound. Aljasim et al. 2025 (100 N at the MC5 head, about 4.4 N m) is a second, stiffer end-range point. Without a spring the muscles' passive force (mostly FDP5) cups the relaxed hand to about 10 / 21 deg.
